summary: Reviewed shared/workflow-manifest.json and shared/workflow-manifest.schema.json against all four Review Dimensions (Maintainability, Best Practices, Security, Future Context).

Cross-referenced all manifest values against mcp-server canonical sources: AGENT_ROLES (constants.ts), PIPELINE_TYPES/DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES/PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP (pipeline-maps.ts), SPEC_VERSION '2.4.1' (constants.ts), inline constants MAX_REWORK_COUNT=5/STALE_PIPELINE_HOURS=24/MAX_HANDOFF_DEPTH=50/handoff_depth_multiplier=30. All 9 role names, 6 pipeline types, ordering, and default_stages match exactly.

Schema is correctly authored for Draft-07: exclusiveMinimum as numeric (not boolean flag), additionalProperties: false at all levels, uniqueItems: true on arrays, correct oneOf for nullable string fields. Structural/semantic validation split is well-documented and appropriate.

No blocking issues found. One non-blocking schema documentation precision: the pipeline field description states 'null for orchestrating roles' but the pm role has orchestrating: false with pipeline: null — description should be updated to 'null for orchestrating roles or roles that do not own a pipeline.'

comments.note: shared/workflow-manifest.json: The prerequisites section encodes the full 6-stage chain (code-review requires security-audit, release-engineering requires code-review). This correctly differs from the legacy PIPELINE_PREREQUISITES static map in pipeline-maps.ts (which has code-review: 'qa'). Downstream consumers of the manifest's prerequisites section must use dynamic per-WP stage filtering (as resolvePrerequisite() does) rather than treating prerequisites as directly applicable to all WP configurations.

shared/workflow-manifest.schema.json: The pipeline field description says 'null for orchestrating roles' which is imprecise — the pm role has orchestrating: false yet pipeline: null. Suggest updating to: 'null for orchestrating roles or roles that do not own a pipeline (e.g. Project Manager).' No validation impact, documentation only.

No further observations — both files are clean, well-structured declarative data files. Schema is correctly split between structural constraints (enforced by AJV) and semantic cross-reference checks (deferred to validate-workflow-manifest.js per WP-005).
